text: This source clearly distinguishes two separate bacterial rice diseases with confirmed scientific names, resolving the earlier flagged uncertainty from a previous batch about which one a given Khmer description referred to. Bacterial leaf blight (ជំងឺរលាកស្លឹក), caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae, begins as water-soaked lesions along the leaf margin that enlarge over time, turning yellow and then whitish-grey as they dry out; in severe cases whole leaves wither. It is most common where a field's irrigation or floodwater comes from an already-infected field, or where infected stubble or weed hosts have been left standing. Control: use resistant varieties; soak seed in sun-warmed water before sowing to help kill surface-borne bacteria that would otherwise be carried onto the seed; apply balanced fertilizer and avoid excess nitrogen; avoid overly dense transplanting; plough and sun-dry the field promptly after harvest; and remove infected plants and weed hosts from the field. Bacterial leaf streak (ជំងឺឆួតស្លឹក), caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola, shows a visually different symptom: narrow, translucent, yellow-orange streaks running lengthwise between the leaf veins, which darken and dry out as the disease progresses. It is most common from the tillering stage onward and spreads faster in hot, humid weather. Control follows the same general principles as leaf blight: resistant varieties, warm-water seed treatment, balanced fertilizer, avoiding dense planting, and clearing infected residue from the field before re-flooding for the next crop. Both diseases are favored by the presence of infected weed or stubble hosts in or around the field, waterborne bacteria carried in irrigation water or canals, hot and humid weather with frequent rain, and excess nitrogen fertilizer. This entry confirms and supersedes the earlier `disease_bacterial_streak_or_blight_FLAGGED.json` item - both diseases are now identified with confirmed scientific names from a clean, legible source rather than left as an unresolved guess.
